content.text: Big A (打大A, dǎ dà A) is a Chinese climbing game for exactly 5 players with variable partnerships, played with two standard 54-card decks (108 cards total including 4 Jokers). Before play, one player exposes an Ace to become the 'declarer' — the holder of the identical Ace (same rank and suit from the other deck) becomes their secret partner. Nobody knows who the partner is until they choose to reveal themselves. If the declarer holds both copies, they play alone against four opponents. Teams score based on the order in which their members empty their hands.

Big A originated in Inner Mongolia, China. It belongs to the large family of Chinese climbing games (shēng jí / 升级 family) that includes Dou Di Zhu and Tractor. The game's distinctive feature is the secret partnership mechanic based on matching identical Aces across two decks.
Two standard 54-card decks (2 × 52 + 4 Jokers = 108 cards). Each deck has a red Joker and a black Joker. Suits are irrelevant except for identifying matching Aces.

Cards are drawn one at a time (as in other Chinese games). Players look at cards as they draw, except for the very last card drawn, which is kept face down temporarily. First three players get 22 cards; last two get 21. Play direction is anti-clockwise.

items.text: Bǎo Huáng (保皇) — Related Game: A related Chinese climbing game with a similar secret-partner mechanic, using a different partnership determination method.
